subject.title: [Feature]: Feature Request: Batch Tool Calls + Context Block Management + Plan Enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw split this umbrella into native tool batching, AI-callable context lifecycle, and plan/workflow enforcement tracks, and which pieces belong in core runtime/API versus plugin or ClawHub surfaces?
rationale: The request adds native tool schemas, persisted context semantics, new config/settings, and runner enforcement policy; repository policy treats those as compatibility- and product-sensitive decisions rather than a narrow repair.

options.title: Split Into Design Tracks
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and require separate maintainer-reviewed designs for batching, context lifecycle, and plan enforcement before implementation.

options.title: Make Narrow Issues Canonical
options.body: Use the existing context and workflow-mode issues for their portions and open or identify a separate native-batching tracker if maintainers want independent ownership.

options.title: Reject Core Orchestration Expansion
options.body: Close or narrow the umbrella if maintainers decide AI-controlled context blocks and strict plan gating duplicate existing agent/tool infrastructure too much for core.

recommendation.title: Split Into Design Tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and require separate maintainer-reviewed designs for batching, context lifecycle, and plan enforcement before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest adjacent history across planning, strict-agentic execution, web search, and context pruning, making him the best available routing owner for the product split.
